I didn't change any code. I can't run Zoom from here to test it, but the code shows this isn't a bug. The black box is the app's **Undetectable** mode working as designed.

When `isUndetectable` is on, the app calls `setContentProtection(true)` on every window: the main window, overlay, settings, model selector and cropper (`electron/main.ts:319-322` at startup, `electron/main.ts:3241-3245` when you toggle it). This tells the operating system to keep those windows out of screen capture. Depending on your OS and Zoom's capture method, a protected window shows up for viewers as a black rectangle or doesn't appear at all. Your "black box" is that protection.

Undetectable mode is off by default (`electron/main.ts:303`), so it must have been switched on at some point. The setting is saved and survives restarts.

**To fix it:**
1. Open the app's **Settings**.
2. Find the card that says **"Undetectable"** with the line *"Natively is currently undetectable by screen-sharing"* (`src/components/SettingsOverlay.tsx:1383-1408`).
3. Turn it off. It should then read **"Detectable"**.

The change applies straight away to all open windows. If Zoom still shows black, stop and restart your screen share so it picks up the windows again.

Turning it off also stops a related behaviour: in Undetectable mode, the app hides its main window whenever Zoom is running (`electron/main.ts:3357-3377`). If your notes window seemed to disappear when Zoom opened, this was the cause too.

If it's already set to "Detectable" and viewers still see black, tell me your OS and whether you share your whole screen or a single window, and I'll look further.
